summary: Changes the message type number for the Terminal Endpoint Identifier Query Request in the ISDN IUA protocol, because the old number clashed with one used by the DUA extension. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Two protocols accidentally used the same number for different messages. This gives one of them a new number so they stop getting mixed up.

questions: what is the iua tei query message type
why did rfc 5133 change message type 5 to 8
subtitle: A one-number fix: the ISDN IUA TEI Query Request message moves from type 5 to type 8 to stop clashing with DUA.

tldr.problem: RFC 4233 gave the TEI Query Request message the type 5, but the DUA extension in RFC 4129 already used type 5 for a DLC Status message, so the two could not be told apart.
tldr.mechanism: This document says TEI Query messages MUST be encoded with message type 8 instead of 5, and IANA reserved type 8 for them.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 4233 and is a Proposed Standard with no replacement listed.

today: RFC 5133 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4233. No later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The ISDN Q.921-User Adaptation Layer (IUA) is described in RFC 3057, which has no Terminal Endpoint Identifier (TEI) Query Request message. The DPNSS/DASS 2 Extensions (DUA) in RFC 4129 add Data Link Connection (DLC) Status messages of types 5, 6 and 7.

Then RFC 4233 updated RFC 3057 and introduced the TEI Query Request message, also using type 5. That made it impossible to tell a DLC Status request from a TEI Query Request.
sections.plainLanguage: Two different messages ended up with the same number, so a receiver could not tell which one it got.

sections.title: The Message Type Change
sections.content: The whole change is one rule: TEI Query messages MUST be encoded with a message type of 8 instead of 5 as described in RFC 4233. Nothing else in RFC 4233 is altered by this document.
sections.plainLanguage: The rule is simple: the TEI Query message now uses number 8, not 5.

sections.title: IANA Registry Entry
sections.content: In the Message Types section of the Signaling User Adaptation Layer Assignments registry, IANA has reserved message type 8 of Management Messages for TEI Query Request messages. This keeps the registry consistent with the new encoding.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list of numbers now shows 8 as taken by the TEI Query message.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document does not require any security considerations in addition to the ones given in RFC 4233, because it only renumbers one message type.
sections.plainLanguage: Changing a label number does not add any new danger.
